draft.title: Alzheimer's disease and memory
card: Alzheimer's disease is a disease of the brain that destroys neurons (nerve cells) over time. Memory problems are often the first sign.
sticky clumps of a protein called beta-amyloid that build up between neurons and disrupt how they communicate.
twisted strands of a protein called tau that build up inside neurons. They stop the neuron working and it eventually dies.

The damage often starts in the hippocampus, which is needed to form new memories. So episodic memory, for personal events, is often lost first. A person may forget this morning's visit but still know a well-known fact.
draft.remember: Plaques sit outside neurons, tangles sit inside them, and both damage neurons. Episodic memory is often lost first.

a.q: Which description matches the tangles seen in Alzheimer's disease?
opts: Twisted tau protein inside neurons that stops them working
Clumps of beta-amyloid between neurons that disrupt signals
Twisted beta-amyloid inside neurons that stops them working
Clumps of tau protein between neurons that disrupt signals
a.why: Tangles are twisted strands of tau protein inside neurons. The option about clumps of beta-amyloid between neurons describes plaques, which sit outside neurons.
a.clue: Think about where tangles sit and which protein forms them.

b.q: Tom, aged 74, is in the early stage of Alzheimer's disease. He cannot recall his grandson's birthday party last weekend, but he can still say that Canberra is the capital of Australia. Which explanation fits best?
opts: Episodic memory is often affected first, before facts
Semantic memory is often affected first, before events
Both memory types are always lost at the same time
Plaques have damaged only his memory for facts
b.why: The party is a personal event, so it is episodic memory, which is often lost first because the hippocampus is damaged early. Knowing the capital is semantic memory, which is often kept longer. The idea that semantic memory goes first reverses this.
b.clue: Which type of memory holds personal events, and which holds facts?

a.best: Twisted tau protein inside neurons that stops them working

b.best: Episodic memory is often affected first, before facts
